resourceName: Burwood Landfill Gas to Queen Elizabeth II Park
description: The purpose of the project is to capture and burn landfill gas from the Burwood Landfill, which has been receiving waste since 1984 and has been closed in June 2005. Roughly half of the waste disposed in the landfill is organic waste that is able to emit methane up to an estimated peak of 1,200 m3 per hour for the next 20 – 30 years. The methane is currently being emitted into the atmosphere leading to an increase in greenhouse gas emissions of up to 140,000 tonnes of CO2e per year (based on a peak of around 1,100 m3 per hour of methane). The project activity involves the installation of equipment to capture, treat and transport methane gas to a nearby swimming pool facility at Queen Elizabeth II Park (QE II Park) where 1,500,000 litres of liquid petroleum gas (LPG) were consumed each year to heat the air and water at the public swimming pool. The project aims to substitute the LPG with landfill gas and to install a co-generation plant to generate electricity for the facility.
